summary: Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Leipzig, studying under Ernst Windisch and August Conrady, and held Leipzig's chair of Indian Philology from 1938 to 1958.

Friedrich Wilhelm worked in Indology and Tibetology. He completed his doctorate at the University of Munich, studying under Paul Thieme, and served at Munich as a Privatdozent in 1963 and as professor from 1969 to 1998.

Friedrich Wilhelm Graf is a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Augsburg from around 1992 to 1999 and at the University of Munich from around 1999 to 2014.

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling was a philosopher who studied at Tübingen and Leipzig. He was a professor at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Berlin (1841–1845), and served as president of the Bavarian Academy.

Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig, earning his Ph.D., and directed the East Asian department of the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1906 to 1928.

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics and classical philology. After earning his Dr. phil. at Halle-Wittenberg, he served as professor at Breslau (1834), professor and rector at Bonn (1839), and professor at Leipzig (ca. 1865–1875).

Friedrich Windischmann studied Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earning doctorates at Bonn and Munich under August Wilhelm von Schlegel and Christian Lassen. He held an extraordinary professorship at Munich (1838–1839) before serving as Vicar General in Munich.

Friedrich Zarncke worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at Rostock and Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt, later serving at the University of Leipzig as a Privatdozent in 1852 and as Rektor from 1869 to 1882.

Friedrich von Adelung was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Leipzig. In 1824, he became director of both the School of Oriental Languages in Saint Petersburg and the University of Vienna.

Friedrich von Spiegel specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology fields. He studied under Friedrich Rückert, Christian Lassen, and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer at Erlangen, Bonn, and Leipzig, and served as professor of Oriental languages at Erlangen from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He earned degrees at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University, later holding professorships at the University of Amsterdam (1962–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (1968–1991).

Fritz Burg was an Indologist and scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin (ca. 1881–1885). He worked at the Hamburg State and University Library, serving as librarian from 1907 to 1926.

Fritz Georg Wolff worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the universities of Munich, Heidelberg, Berlin, and Giessen, where he completed his Ph.D. under Christian Bartholomae around 1903 to 1905.

Fritz Hommel was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig and Munich under Friedrich Delitzsch and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, subsequently holding a post at the University of Munich from around 1877 to 1925.
Fritz Hungerleider was an Austrian scholar in Buddhist studies who attended the Handelsakademie. He served as president of the Buddhistische Gesellschaft from 1955 to 1975.

Fritz Johaentgen was an Indologist who studied at Bonn and Berlin under Christian Lassen, Martin Haug, Albrecht Weber, and Franz Bopp. He earned his Ph.D. at Berlin and served there as a Privatdozent from 1864 to 1878.

Fritz Kern worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his Ph.D. at Berlin, he taught at Kiel, became an ordinary professor at Frankfurt (1914–1922), and served as a professor at the University of Bonn (ca. 1925–1947).

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied and habilitated at the University of Munich. He held a professorship at Bonn (1934), taught at Munich (1936–1941), and held a chair at the University of Mainz from around 1946 to 1969.

Frédéric Baudry specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at the École Normale Supérieure and under Eugène Burnouf. He worked as a librarian at Versailles and the Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, serving as administrator of the Bibliothèque Mazarine from 1874 to 1885.

Frédéric Richard works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Lausanne and the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, later working as coordinator at Lausanne (2015–2019) and project manager at the Centre intercantonal d'information sur les croyances (2020).
